title: Four more test binaries were attached only to narrow opt-in steps and never executed; two of them fail on first run (iss105_token_model_test GIN index, differential_test)
discovered_during: WF03-gh439-testwiring-20260806 step q150 (ISS-0150 / GH #466) — found by the new unattached-run-artifact check added to tools/lint_test_wiring.py
symptom:
ISS-0150(B) was not a one-off. Strengthening tools/lint_test_wiring.py to verify that every addTest Run artifact is reachable from an aggregate build step (`test` / `test-integration`) found four more test binaries in exactly the same shape — created, fully configured, and attached only to a narrow `test-integration-<slug>` step that nothing in the pipeline invokes:

  run_xc04_integration_tests                 tests/integration/xc04_kernel_determinism_test.zig      (5 blocks)
  run_stage11_sim_xc04_integration_tests     tests/integration/stage11_sim_xc04_aggregate_test.zig   (1 block)
  run_iss105_integration_tests               tests/integration/iss105_token_model_test.zig           (4 blocks)
  run_differential_tests                     tests/differential/differential_test.zig                (3 blocks)

13 test blocks in total that never ran under `zig build test` or `zig build test-integration`.

The first two pass on first execution and were attached to test_integration_others_step under ISS-0150. The remaining two FAIL on first execution and are the subject of this issue:

  zig build test-integration-iss105  -> 3 pass, 1 fail
      'iss105_token_model: active_tokens has GIN index' failed
  zig build test-differential        -> exit 1
root_cause:
Two separable causes.

(1) Build-graph: a `test-integration-<slug>` narrow step is an opt-in convenience for running one binary during development. Attaching a Run artifact ONLY to such a step leaves it unreachable from the aggregate steps CI actually invokes, so its tests never run in practice. There is no convention or gate that required the barrier attachment as well, so the omission was invisible — the same omission as ISS-0150(B).

(2) The two failing binaries: their failures have never been diagnosed because the tests have never executed. The iss105 failure asserts a GIN index on `active_tokens` that the current schema does not appear to provide; the differential suite's failure is not yet triaged.
reproduction:
python tools/lint_test_wiring.py     # reports both as [KNOWN], tracked by this issue
  zig build test-integration-iss105    # 3 pass, 1 fail — 'active_tokens has GIN index'
  zig build test-differential          # exit 1
impact:
MAJOR rather than BLOCKER: the two files still unattached hold 7 test blocks whose subject matter (ISS-105 token model indexing, differential engine comparison) is covered in part elsewhere, and no production defect is yet confirmed behind either failure. But until they are diagnosed, whatever they are detecting stays undetected, and the ISS-105 GIN-index assertion in particular may indicate a real missing index on a hot query path.

The wider point: this is the second instance of the 'attached to a narrow step only' pattern found in one week, at a rate of four occurrences per audit. It is a systemic build-graph convention gap, not a series of individual mistakes.
candidate_resolution:
For each of the two remaining binaries:
  1. Diagnose the first-run failure (do NOT relax the assertion to make it pass — for iss105, determine whether the GIN index on active_tokens should exist and add the migration if so).
  2. Once green, add `test_integration_others_step.dependOn(&<run_name>.step);` (or the `test` step equivalent for the differential suite).
  3. Remove the artifact's entry from KNOWN_UNATTACHED in tools/lint_test_wiring.py — the ledger must shrink to empty.

Separately, consider documenting in docs/guides/test_infrastructure_guide.md that a narrow `test-integration-<slug>` step is always in ADDITION to the barrier attachment, never instead of it. The linter now enforces this, but the convention should be written down where authors of new build.zig targets will read it.
notes:
Filed separately from ISS-0150 rather than folded into it. ISS-0150's scope was two named files that report green without testing anything; that is discharged. These four are a distinct population found BY the tooling improvement ISS-0150 motivated, and the two that remain need their own diagnose/fix cycle because each will surface behaviour questions (is the GIN index actually required?) that a build-graph fix cannot answer.

The two failing binaries are deliberately NOT attached to the barrier yet, and are deliberately NOT skipped or deleted. They are recorded in an explicit KNOWN_UNATTACHED ledger in tools/lint_test_wiring.py that prints them on every run as [KNOWN] with this issue id. That keeps `zig build test` gating on the new check today without hiding what the check found — the alternative (attach and leave `zig build test` red, or suppress silently) would either block the whole pipeline or recreate the invisibility this issue is about.
resolution: Both orphaned test binaries fixed and attached to aggregate steps, emptying the KNOWN_UNATTACHED ledger in tools/lint_test_wiring.py. differential_tests never compiled: @embedFile("../../src/engine/transition.zig") cannot escape the embedding module's root, so the bytes now arrive via the new src/engine/transition_source_embed.zig shim; 3/3 pass and it is attached to `test` (service-free, so the Green-Main Gate keeps its no-services property). iss105_integration_tests passes 4/4 as written -- its GIN-index assertion creates the index it then asserts on, so it was never the real defect; attached to test_integration_others_step. Verified: zig build exit 0, zig build test exit 0 with the wiring gate active, lint_test_wiring exit 0 reporting an empty ledger.
prevention: lint_test_wiring.py now checks step-ATTACHMENT in addition to reachability, so a binary that is built but hangs off no aggregate step is caught. The KNOWN_UNATTACHED ledger is a visible temporary record printed on every run, never a silent suppression, and it must return to empty.
